title: Volume of Prisms, Pyramids, Cylinders, Cones and Spheres
standard_text: G.11D apply the formulas for the volume of three-dimensional figures, including prisms, pyramids, cones, cylinders, spheres, and composite figures, to solve problems using appropriate units of measure
meta_desc: Free Geometry volume worksheets for Texas TEKS G.11D: volume of prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones, spheres and composite solids. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Prism Bh; pyramid ⅓Bh; sphere 4/3 πr³.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Prism and cylinder: V = Bh (cylinder: πr2h).
  • Pyramid and cone: V = ⅓Bh (cone: ⅓πr2h).
  • Sphere: V = 43πr3. Hemisphere: half of that.
  • Composite solids: add or subtract the parts.

Examples

Example

Cone: radius 3, height 10

⅓ × π × 9 × 10

Answer: 30π

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting ⅓Cones and pyramids are a third of a prism.
Using the diameter as the radiusHalve the diameter.
Cubing the wrong numberOnly r is cubed for a sphere.

items.e: Cavalieri's principle: same height and the same cross-section at every level means the same volume. π × 14² × 38 = 7,448π. They are equal (7,448π mm³ each).
